conviction_note: Two forces of similar size offset: the company has beaten its own quarterly revenue guide by 33% (Q1) and 63% (Q2) and raised the FY guide at every print, which argues for another large beat and raise. Against that, the stock already sits at $42.97, above every published price target ($32-40), up 18.9% in 20 sessions and about 18% since 9 Oct with no company news found, and option OI is almost all calls (P/C OI 0.02), so a beat looks expected. TruStage, a top-3 carrier, is still only partly restored as of 2 Nov, which adds a persistency and guide risk. impact_sum +0.2 and scaled +0.88 agree in sign and size: both are near-zero leans on a name that will move about 22 points either way.
bar: Company Q3 2026 guide: revenue $160-164m, adj. EBITDA $23-25m; FY26 revenue $727-731m, adj. EBITDA $119-123m (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm, 2026-08-03). Sell-side revenue consensus $163.3m, at the guide top (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LIFE/earnings-forecasts). The EPS consensus is disputed: $0.30-0.31 on Benzinga against $0.09 on TheRightTrader/Earnings Whispers, so EPS is not used as a bar. The revenue bar is sourced to the guide and a consensus that agrees with it. The real buy-side whisper is unsourced and almost certainly well above the guide, given Q1 ($145m guide, $193m actual) and Q2 ($116m guide, $189.6m actual). print_vs_bar_pct +13 is measured against the $163.3m consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,113,640 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 6.5% of float, 2.87 days to cover, up from 1,819,799 (3.0%) on 2026-09-15 and 3,710,794 on 2026-09-30 (MarketBeat/FINRA, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LIFE/short-interest/, data published 2026-10-26). That is rising but not crowded. Baseline: 25-delta skew +5.37 vol points (downside paid, modest); ATM IV 134.5%; event-implied move 23.79%; put/call open interest 0.02 (29,116 total OI, almost entirely calls), which is call-heavy long positioning. Spot $42.97 is 2.8% below the 52-week high and 336% above the 52-week low. Run-up: +1.58% over 5 days, +18.93% over 20 days.

findings.finding: Ethos has beaten its own quarterly revenue guide by a wide margin twice since the IPO: Q1 2026 guide $144-146m against $193m actual (+33%), and Q2 guide $114-118m against $189.6m actual (+63%, consensus $117.3m). The Q3 guide of $160-164m sits $26-30m below Q2's actual, and the sell-side consensus of $163.3m sits on the guide, so the published bar is again the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 beat (+33% vs guide): stock +32.3% close-to-close (2026-05-06 amc). Q2 beat (+63% vs guide) with an FY raise: +21.1% (2026-08-03 amc). Q4 2025 (first print, 2026-02-25): +3.7%. Beats have been bought, on only 3 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The sell-side consensus ($163.3m) still anchors on the guide, which would look different if the street had modelled the beat pattern. But the price has largely done it: the stock is above every price target and up ~18% since 9 Oct with no company news, which is what a priced-in large beat looks like. The edge left is only whether the beat clears the buy-side whisper, and that whisper is unsourced, so the finding is sized small against a 24-point implied move.
findings.independence: Q1 guide/actual: https://ethos.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/ethos-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results (2026-05-06) and Q4 2025 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788451/000119312526071749/d109531dex991.htm (2026-02-25). These are the company's own documents, so not independent of the company; there is no independent Q3 volume series (carriers Ameritas and TruStage are mutuals, Banner Life is private).

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide has been raised at every print: $510-514m (Feb), $561-565m (May), $727-731m (Aug). The current FY guide implies Q4 revenue of about $184m and H2 of $346m, against H1's $383m. A repeat of the pattern means another FY raise, and the 2027 outlook is deferred to February.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Both FY raises (May, Aug) came with +32% and +21% moves, but those also carried the quarter beat, so the guide's own contribution cannot be separated on 3 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The implied Q4 of ~$184m is a guide figure the sell side carries, and a large raise would visibly lift FY estimates. But the raise pattern is public and the stock already sits above every price target, so only the size of the raise relative to the buy-side expectation is unpriced. The CFO's 'skinnier' third-party economics and growth investments make an EBITDA raise smaller than a revenue raise.
findings.independence: Shares the beat-and-raise pattern with finding 1, but rests on a different line (the FY guide, not the quarter). FY history from https://ethos.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/ethos-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788451/000119312526071749/d109531dex991.htm.

findings.finding: TruStage, one of the three carriers (with Ameritas and Banner Life) that made up ~88% of Ethos revenue in H1 2026, suspended almost all financial services from 14 July after a cyber attack. As of 2 Nov its outage page (status 'Investigating') still shows only phased resumption of recurring payments, no online one-time payments, and grace periods to be extended so that 'more than one premium may come due'. Ethos's 16 Sep 8-K reassured only on the July billing cycle ('no incremental lapse rates') and said the impact was in the Q3 guide. Ethos recognises estimated renewal commissions upfront using persistency estimates: $293m non-current commissions receivable at 30 June.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print carried a persistency revision except Q1's $16.5m non-cash charge on third-party agent compensation estimates, which was buried in a +33% beat and a +32.3% move. Stock was ~$36-40 around the 16 Sep 8-K.
findings.why_not_priced: The incident is public and Ethos addressed it on 16 Sep, so the headline is priced. What is not visibly priced is the duration: the company's assurance covered one billing cycle, while TruStage is still not billing normally three and a half months later. If the market had priced a persistency write-down or a TruStage volume drag, the stock would not be at the 52-week high above every target. Sized small, net of the rest of the company: TruStage is one of three carriers, Ameritas and Banner can absorb volume, and the company says Q3 is guided for it. Any lapse catch-up may only surface after payment processing fully resumes, which could be after the window.
findings.independence: Ethos 8-K 2026-09-16: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788451/000119312526392523/d24330d8k.htm. Wikipedia on TruStage, 'as of the beginning of October 2026, services remained incompletely operational': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TruStage_Financial_Group. Commissions receivable from the 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526335209/life-20260630.htm. These are three different sources.

findings.finding: The stock has outrun the sell side: spot $42.97 against published targets of JPM $37 (downgraded to Neutral on valuation, ~1 Oct), Barclays $37, BofA $38, Goldman $35, Citi $33, Citizens JMP $33, and Deutsche Bank $40 as the highest. It is up from $36.50 on 9 Oct with no company news found, 2.8% off the 52-week high, with call-dominated option OI (P/C 0.02).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before both large positive reactions the stock was not extended: ~$21.7 on 15 May (pre-Q1 ~$15-19) and $20.42 on 31 Jul against a ~$33 target set later. This is the first print entered above consensus targets, so there is no precedent.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is a statement about what is priced rather than an unpriced fact: the run-up plus call-heavy OI says a large beat and raise is expected. It is sized as the reaction-function risk that a beat in line with the pattern sells. The rising short interest (1.8m to 4.1m shares since mid-Sep, 6.5% of float) is not crowded enough to make a squeeze the dominant mechanism, but it partly offsets, so the size is kept small.
findings.independence: Run-up and OI from the sealed baseline; short interest https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/LIFE/short-interest/ (published 2026-10-26). These are different sources from the target list.

findings.finding: Margin and mix: the Q3 adj. EBITDA guide of $23-25m (~15% margin at the midpoint) is below Q2's $35.2m (19%). The CFO attributes this to a higher third-party mix with 'skinnier' unit economics (third-party +90% y/y in Q2, direct share down 14 points Q1 to Q2) and to strategic growth investments. An $8m carrier-settlement cash timing benefit in Q2 operating cash flow reverses in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 margin compression (direct share down 14 pts) came with +21.1%, so the market looked through mix at the last print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is inside what the company guided, so it is mostly priced. The small residual is quality-of-beat risk: a revenue beat on third-party mix with weaker EBITDA conversion, and a weak Q3 operating cash flow from the $8m reversal. JPM's downgrade already names lower cash-flow conversion, so this is partly in the price.
findings.independence: Q3 EBITDA guide in the 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001788451/000119312526330556/life-ex99_1.htm; JPM on cash conversion https://beinsure.com/news/jpmorgan-downgrades-ethos-technologies-stock-life-to-neutral/.

Wang still holds 1.54m Class A and 3.69m Class B shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Heavy Form 4/144 activity in Aug-Sep after the Q2 print coincided with the stock holding ~$34-40; no measurable reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and on a pre-set plan, so it carries almost no information about the quarter. Filed small, for completeness, as supply above $37.

findings.finding: Industry backdrop: LIMRA's Q2 2026 US term life new premium rose 7% to $829m (policy count +6%), and LIMRA expects 2026 term sales roughly flat. Ethos's own Q2 policy count grew 133%, so its growth is share gain and distribution expansion, not market growth. No Q3 2026 industry release was out.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none; the industry series has never been tied to an LIFE move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy that does not bear on Ethos's company-specific growth; filed at 0 as a broad series showing no headwind.

outside_window.finding: On 9 Oct Ethos filed an updated beneficial-ownership table 'in connection with the December 2026 reconstitution of the Russell indices': 41.7m Class A and 23.3m Class B shares outstanding at 30 Sep. Possible index-inclusion demand is dated December, after the exit window.

TruStage lapse catch-up: once TruStage resumes normal billing and grace periods end, multiple premiums fall due at once, which could raise lapses and force a persistency revision on Ethos's TruStage book. Timing depends on TruStage's recovery and likely falls in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 reporting.

rejected_candidates.detail: Its accounting point (upfront renewal recognition on persistency estimates) is the channel through which finding 3 (TruStage persistency) acts. The report itself is 5 months old and was followed by a +21% Q2 reaction.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 4 (stock above all price targets) and finding 5 (cash conversion).

rejected_candidates.detail: The authorisation is in the same Q2 release as findings 1-2 and was announced with the +21% reaction. No Q3 repurchase figure exists before the print, so there is nothing new to size separately.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The beat-and-raise pattern cuts against the modest put skew (+5.37) and points up, while the +18.9% 20-day run-up, a price above every target and call-heavy OI say that pattern is already priced. The net lean is near zero, slightly positive.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): the TruStage finding rests on one of three carriers, which Ameritas and Banner can offset, and the company says it is in the Q3 guide. Shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0.

Lesson 6 (bar): the revenue bar is sourced to the guide and an agreeing consensus. The EPS bar is disputed ($0.09 vs $0.30), so no finding uses it. The buy-side whisper is unsourced, so the beat finding stays small (+2.5) against a 24-point implied move. No change in size.

Lessons 1 and 7: the name has bought its beats (+32%, +21%) and the short interest (6.5%, 2.9 DTC) is not crowded, so the positioning negative stays at -2.0. The near-zero net sign does not fight the modest skew. No change.
Lesson 5: the LIMRA industry proxy stays filed at 0, not dropped.
Everything else stood. Post-lessons impact_sum is +0.2 against -0.3 pre-lessons; abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
